description: GroundwaterCast UK is an independent open-source forecasting workflow for monitored boreholes in England. It combines Environment Agency observations, ECMWF rainfall ensembles and Copernicus weather and seasonal products with calibrated Pastas recharge models. It publishes a 14-day probabilistic groundwater-level fan, an experimental six-month outlook and some river low-flow forecasts through an artefact pack and map interface. The README reports about 1,378 monitored boreholes, of which 687 have full forecasts, and 94 river gauges at its review date. Geographic coverage is England; forecast horizons are 14 days and six months. MIT source is public, but reproducing the complete pipeline requires a free Copernicus account and acceptance of separate data terms. A major limitation, stated by the maintainer, is that forecast uncertainty remains uncalibrated until an archived winter is verified. It can help evaluate groundwater stress for water supply and drought-sensitive assets. The catalogue's data-era5-reanalysis is one distinct weather source. No forecast artefact or input dataset was downloaded.
